definition: critical c p sums welfare minus c for each individual. For c>0, adding a life with 0<w<c strictly reduces critical score despite increasing ordinary total; c/2 refutes universal positive-life scoring. This policy and average welfare are formal alternatives with distinct mere-addition costs, not normative recommendations.
